`order_problems()` enforces only 2 pairs (design_review<gate1, diff_review<gate2); AC requires failing any pre-merge stage missing **or out of order** — planning→gate0→implementation→code_review→tests→precheck chain order is never verified.

Lock staleness threshold (60s) exceeds acquire timeout (10s): a crashed writer makes every subsequent `record()` time out for ≥60s, generating failure-sink entries that then block completion.

`REQUIRED_AT_COMPLETION` includes `completion`, but the AC's pre-merge list excludes it — precheck fails any item not yet passed through `set_status(completed)`, forcing an awkward status-before-precheck order.

`gate0_check` and `precheck._record_trail` append planning/gate0/code_review/tests/precheck on every run with no dedup — trails grow unboundedly until `MAX_EVENTS` RuntimeError, which itself routes to the failure sink and blocks the item.

`execution-trail` is registered in precheck `_GATES` (tier "post") **and** executed manually after `_record_trail` — double execution, and the `_GATES` copy can run before tests/precheck events exist, yielding false FAILs.
`_record_trail` records `tests`/`code_review` as "pass" with empty rows when no matching gate ran (`all([]) == True`) — fabricated pass evidence.

`gate_decisions` always records `status="pass"` regardless of decision — a REJECT/DEFER decision shows as passing trail evidence.

The evidence store's failure sink and lock design create self-perpetuating blocks: transient errors become permanent, unremovable completion failures.

Repeated per-run appends and duplicated failure-handling boilerplate will degrade maintainability and evidence integrity as adoption grows; fix dedup, single execution of the gate, and a shared write helper before relying on this as audit evidence.
